description: T-5422: does Excel for the web calculate ECMA.CEILING stored without its _xlfn. prefix? Desktop Excel 16 saves the name bare (calipers roundtrip/formula_stress_test Math!B17, cached 2), and T-1301 recorded that Graph refused a workbook holding the bare name (createSession 501 unsupportedWorkbook), in a workbook that may also have held the one-argument call. Sheet S holds the bare call alone: A1 is the value, A2 its error type through IFERROR (0 for a value, 5 for #NAME?). Both cells are listed in bare_function_names, so the builder writes ECMA.CEILING without the prefix. Neither is scored: they ask how a stored (file) formula loads, while the engine reads the spec text as a typed formula, where ECMA.CEILING is the function; their oracle values are the evidence (docs/excel-semantics/numbers.md "ECMA.CEILING"). If the session is refused, that refusal is the answer: record it in the fill's log and in docs/excel-semantics/numbers.md under ECMA.CEILING. The prefixed form is probes/ecma-ceiling A1 (4). Precision!B2:B4 must retain 0.9999999999999998, 1, 1.0000000000000002; C2:C4 must be -1,0,1.
